/**
 * @dev Interface of the ERC20 Permit extension allowing approvals to be made via signatures, as defined in
 * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612[EIP-2612].
 *
 * Adds the {permit} method, which can be used to change an account's ERC20 allowance (see {IERC20-allowance}) by
 * presenting a message signed by the account. By not relying on `{IERC20-approve}`, the token holder account doesn't
 * need to send a transaction, and thus is not required to hold Ether at all.
 */
interface IERC20Permit {
    /**
     * @dev Sets `value` as the allowance of `spender` over `owner`'s tokens,
     * given `owner`'s signed approval.
     *
     * IMPORTANT: The same issues {IERC20-approve} has related to transaction
     * ordering also apply here.
     *
     * Emits an {Approval} event.
     *
     * Requirements:
     *
     * - `spender` cannot be the zero address.
     * - `deadline` must be a timestamp in the future.
     * - `v`, `r` and `s` must be a valid `secp256k1` signature from `owner`
     * over the EIP712-formatted function arguments.
     * - the signature must use ``owner``'s current nonce (see {nonces}).
     *
     * For more information on the signature format, see the
     * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2612#specification[relevant EIP
     * section].
     */
    function permit(address owner, address spender, uint256 value, uint256 deadline, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s) external;

    /**
     * @dev Returns the current nonce for `owner`. This value must be
     * included whenever a signature is generated for {permit}.
     *
     * Every successful call to {permit} increases ``owner``'s nonce by one. This
     * prevents a signature from being used multiple times.
     */
    function nonces(address owner) external view returns (uint256);

    /**
     * @dev Returns the domain separator used in the encoding of the signature for `permit`, as defined by {EIP712}.
     */
    // solhint-disable-next-line func-name-mixedcase
    function DOMAIN_SEPARATOR() external view returns (bytes32);
}

decimals().details: Returns the number of decimals used to get its user representation. For example, if `decimals` equals `2`, a balance of `505` tokens should be displayed to a user as `5,05` (`505 / 10 ** 2`). Tokens usually opt for a value of 18, imitating the relationship between Ether and Wei. This is the value {ERC20} uses, unless {_setupDecimals} is called. NOTE: This information is only used for _display_ purposes: it in no way affects any of the arithmetic of the contract, including {IERC20-balanceOf} and {IERC20-transfer}.

decreaseAllowance(address,uint256).details: Atomically decreases the allowance granted to `spender` by the caller. This is an alternative to {approve} that can be used as a mitigation for problems described in {IERC20-approve}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address. - `spender` must have allowance for the caller of at least `subtractedValue`.

selectedFunctions.label: Gamma Strategies Withdraw Base WETH-USDC vault liquidity
warnings: Static deployment-bound source/ABI inventory only, not a fresh runtime identity, current pool state, balance, liquidity, backing, successful execution or financial-safety guarantee. Exact grants, canonical calldata, pause overlays and independent controls remain mandatory; zero native value required.

Only current-app Base Aerodrome N WETH-USDC direct Hypervisor 0xa0f688905ef05ea853c35131b4899a613b4ba644 is admitted. Constructor binds pool 0xb2cc224c1c9fee385f8ad6a55b4d94e92359dc59 and reads immutable token0/token1 from it. Official current app maps token0 to 18-decimal Base WETH 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 and token1 to 6-decimal native USDC 0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913, not USDbC. Vault share decimals are 18; share amount is not a fixed raw token amount.

withdraw requires positive shares and nonzero recipient, then ultimately requires from == msg.sender and burns caller shares. Existing LP share allowance or approved operator does not authorize a different from. No LP approval is needed for the owner withdrawal. Outputs go to the explicit to recipient and remain WETH plus USDC, not native ETH.

Four minAmounts are base token0/token1 and limit token0/token1 liquidity burn minimums, not aggregate recipient output minimums. They are checked against amounts owed only for each nonzero liquidity position. Pro-rata unused balances are added afterwards. There is no deadline or aggregate min-output argument; floor rounding can reduce withdrawn position liquidity and dust outputs.

Before withdrawal, zeroBurn settles fees on both ranges, collects them to the vault and pays floor(owed/fee) to mutable feeRecipient. Source initial fee denominator is not asserted as current; owner can change fee without a range check. Zero fee can cause division-by-zero and block operations. Owner rebalancing/ranges, fee recipient, pool dependency and token behavior can affect or revert withdrawal. No onchain generic pause field exists in this exact interface.

Direct Hypervisor deposit is whitelist-only (msg.sender == whitelistedAddress), not ordinary user mint. Official docs route deposits through UniProxy; that separate deposit target is not admitted here. Owner rebalance/compound/liquidity management and ERC20 approvals/transfers/permit are excluded. No arbitrary executor, dynamic hypervisor target, opaque zap, or multicall admitted.

Withdrawal invokes typed burn/collect on constructor-bound immutable pool, not a caller-selected call target or payload. The separate mint callback accepts bytes but requires msg.sender == pool and mintCalled == true and pays configured tokens; it is excluded. No callback authorization or runtime nested-execution language is added.

Current official app identifies this vault under Aerodrome/Base and current official API recognizes the same chain/protocol/address. This is a bounded ordinary withdrawal inventory for a maintained listed vault, not a retired/exit-only deployment admission and not support for all historical Gamma strategies, deposits, incentives or complete workflows.
